candidates.requirement: Enable the repository-supported INI_ALLOW_NO_VALUE mode so the string parser can invoke the handler for a bare name after an earlier parse error.
candidates.target_route: LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput → ini_parse_string → ini_parse_string_length → ini_parse_stream, using a bounded string such as "[broken\nname\n".
candidates.failure_condition: The old recipe supplies no enabling definition, so ini.h sets INI_ALLOW_NO_VALUE to 0 and excludes the handler branch.
candidates.alternative_paths: The target calls only the string parser with this build. With the branch excluded, no generated string, seed, default, or callback result can execute the changed after-error handler behavior.

candidates.requirement: Exercise the bare-name handler failure path after an earlier error, with INI_ALLOW_NO_VALUE enabled and a callback that can reject that bare name.
candidates.target_route: The same string parser receives "[broken\nname\n"; the bare-name handler returns 0 after the first line has set error.
candidates.failure_condition: The recipe excludes the branch, and the old callback always returns 1. Thus no old-target input executes the added first-error guard.
candidates.alternative_paths: The default no-value error branch can preserve an error but never invokes the bare-name handler. Other callback calls cannot exercise this guard.

before.requirement: Cover the supported bare-name handler behavior after an earlier error.
before.reason: The old source also placed bare-name handling under INI_ALLOW_NO_VALUE, which the fixed recipe did not enable. Its additional !error guard prevented the after-error call even in an enabled build.

source_evidence.quote:
/* Stop parsing on first error (default is to keep parsing). */
#ifndef INI_STOP_ON_FIRST_ERROR
#define INI_STOP_ON_FIRST_ERROR 0
#endif

/* Nonzero to call the handler at the start of each new section (with
   name and value NULL). Default is to only call the handler on
   each name=value pair. */
#ifndef INI_CALL_HANDLER_ON_NEW_SECTION
#define INI_CALL_HANDLER_ON_NEW_SECTION 0
#endif

/* Nonzero to allow a name without a value (no '=' or ':' on the line) and
   call the handler with value NULL in this case. Default is to treat
   no-value lines as an error. */
#ifndef INI_ALLOW_NO_VALUE
#define INI_ALLOW_NO_VALUE 0
#endif

after.requirement: Cover the bare-name handler call after an earlier error.
after.reason: The removed !error guard permits that call in an enabled build, but the same target recipe still compiles out the handler branch.

before.requirement: Cover first-error handling when a bare-name callback rejects a later line.
before.reason: The old bare-name handler path was already excluded by the target build, and its callback always returned success. The old !error guard additionally prevented a call after a prior error.

source_evidence.quote:
/* Parse given INI-style file. May have [section]s, name=value pairs
   (whitespace stripped), and comments starting with ';' (semicolon). Section
   is "" if name=value pair parsed before any section heading. name:value
   pairs are also supported as a concession to Python's configparser.

   For each name=value pair parsed, call handler function with given user
   pointer as well as section, name, and value (data only valid for duration
   of handler call). Handler should return nonzero on success, zero on error.

   Returns 0 on success, line number of first error on parse error (doesn't
   stop on first error), -1 on file open error, or -2 on memory allocation
   error (only when INI_USE_STACK is zero).

after.requirement: Cover the added first-error guard when a bare-name callback rejects a later line.
after.reason: The added guard remains inside the disabled no-value branch, and the fixed callback still cannot reject a bare name.
